title: Component pullback coefficient and scalar comparison squares
statement: Let Lambda be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and T a w-contractible affine scheme [sk-def-pe-wlocal]. For the fixed relative test inverse image [def-zl-condensed-lisse-evaluation-model], assume continuity, braidedness and preservation of finite limits and colimits. Then there is a ring-object coefficient isomorphism alpha and a monoidal factorization beta from restriction to pi_0(T) followed by component inverse image to the actual point inverse image, with alpha induced by beta at Lambda. The corresponding componentComparisons hold: triangulated strong symmetric component pullback preserves the unit, induces the lisse equivalence, and carries the actual section-ring realization and both point-scalar realizations to one another by the displayed natural isomorphisms.

proof.text: Use the relative-site factorization and take its adjunction mate on abelian sheaves. Its uniqueness gives monoidal beta and its value at Lambda gives alpha.

Termwise coefficient module pullback is exact. Canonical tensor pullback gives derived strong symmetry and the unit comparison. Clopen refinement and point-basis evaluation identify the two section rings with Lambda(pi_0 T), including constants.

On flat-term K-flat complexes compare pulled-back scalar realizations by the ordinary balanced tensor maps. K-flat preservation and tensor descent give the natural realization square on the whole unbounded derived category.

The component space is extremally disconnected. Apply contractible evaluation on both sites and identify the component functor with scalar transport between perfect categories. This gives the lisse equivalence. Compose the point factorization with the scalar square for the final scalar formula.
